historical_timeline.summary: Born Robert Craig Knievel in Butte, Montana; raised by his grandparents.
Begins his daredevil career with a touring motorcycle show.
Crashes after jumping the fountains at Caesars Palace, Las Vegas, and is hospitalized, by the obituaries' account in a coma for a month.
Rocket-powered attempt to jump Idaho's Snake River Canyon fails.
Breaks his pelvis in the crash landing of a jump over 13 buses at Wembley Stadium; Guinness World Records later counts 433 fractures by the end of the year.
Concussion and two broken arms in a jump attempt in Chicago; retires from major jumps.
Liver transplant after nearly dying of hepatitis C, likely acquired through a transfusion after a crash; reported to have stopped drinking at the time of the transplant.
Dies at 69 in Clearwater, Florida, of natural causes after years of diabetes, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, pain from his injuries and two strokes.

claims.statement: He began his daredevil career in 1965 with a touring motorcycle show. His crash after jumping the fountains at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas, dated 1968 in the wire obituaries, put him in the hospital, by their account in a coma for a month.
claims.clinical_interpretation: One of the crashes behind the many fractures and the chronic pain in the modern episode. The length of the coma is disputed in later accounts.

claims.statement: In 1974 his rocket-powered cycle failed in an attempt to jump Idaho's Snake River Canyon. In 1975 the crash landing of his jump over 13 buses at Wembley Stadium in London broke his pelvis. In the winter of 1976 an attempt to jump a tank of live sharks in Chicago left him with a concussion and two broken arms, after which he retired from major jumps.

synthetic_episode.teaching_objective: Find and treat chronic hepatitis C with cirrhosis in a 57-year-old former stunt performer who received many transfusions before 1962: raised transaminases and low platelets prompt hepatitis C antibody with reflex RNA; staging by FIB-4, elastography and ultrasound, with Child-Pugh and MELD-Na; the AASLD-IDSA simplified pathway for compensated cirrhosis with a pan-genotypic regimen (sofosbuvir-velpatasvir for 12 weeks), hepatitis B testing, a drug interaction check (proton pump inhibitor, statin) and hypoglycemia monitoring; cure confirmed by HCV RNA 12 or more weeks after treatment; Baveno VII use of liver stiffness and platelets to identify clinically significant portal hypertension and treat it with carvedilol instead of screening endoscopy; liver cancer surveillance by ultrasound with alpha-fetoprotein every six months that continues after cure; hepatitis A and B vaccination; transplant referral only if decompensation or a MELD-Na of 15 or more develops; pain care that is safe in cirrhosis (acetaminophen up to 2 g a day, no oral NSAIDs, no opioids, topical treatment, physical and aquatic therapy, sleep and coping skills); diabetes care adapted to cirrhosis, with continuous glucose monitoring because the A1c can read falsely low; alcohol counseling toward abstinence; and fall and fracture prevention, with bone density testing, vitamin D and an intravenous bisphosphonate, on the AASLD-IDSA HCV guidance, the AASLD 1993 HCC guidance, Baveno VII, the AASLD portal hypertension and ascites guidance, the ADA Standards of Care and the CMID diabetes and osteoporosis monographs.

hpi.narrative: Mr. Knievel returns two weeks after his first visit. The hepatitis C antibody was positive and the reflex test found HCV RNA, 2.35 million IU/mL, genotype 1a. Hepatitis B surface antigen, core antibody and surface antibody were all negative, so he has never had hepatitis B and is not immune; hepatitis A IgG was negative; HIV was negative. The ultrasound a week ago showed a nodular liver, a 14.2 cm spleen, no liver mass and no ascites. Dr. Okonkwo of hepatology saw him this morning, and transient elastography in her clinic measured liver stiffness at 26.8 kPa. He stopped ibuprofen and omeprazole after the first visit and uses acetaminophen twice a day and diclofenac gel on his knees; pain is a little worse in the mornings. He has cut down to about two drinks most evenings. He has had no abdominal swelling, black stools, vomiting of blood, confusion or yellow eyes. He has had no thoughts of self-harm.
